title: HTML Interchange Briefing
description: A compact fixture for testing one Capsule with reader, mobile, slides, and mobile story presentations generated from shared sections, cards, and assets.

sections.title: The core idea
sections.body: HTML should become the default interchange surface for moving durable work out of LLM chats and app workflows. A Capsule is the sealed single-file form of that idea: readable by humans, structured for machines, and portable into future LLM contexts.

sections.title: One artifact, four useful views
sections.body: The same content snapshot can be read as a desktop page, a mobile page, a desktop slide deck, or a mobile story sequence. Those are presentations of one substance, not separate artifacts by default.

sections.title: Identity follows the sealed package
sections.body: When the views are generated together at export time, they share one Capsule UUID. When Vault later compiles a new enhanced package from an already sealed Capsule, the new package gets a new UUID and provenance back to the source.

sections.title: Assets live once
sections.body: Heavy media should be stored once and referenced by stable asset ids. Presentations can render the same media differently without duplicating the substance.

assets.alt: Four presentation surfaces derived from one Capsule data model.

cards.title: HTML Interchange
cards.body: One sealed Capsule, multiple ways to read it.

cards.title: HTML is the handoff
cards.body: LLM chats and apps can export work as HTML that humans can inspect and future tools can parse.

cards.title: Four views, one substance
cards.body: Reader, mobile, slides, and story can all render the same sections and cards.

cards.title: UUIDs track packages
cards.body: Views generated together stay in one Capsule. Later enhanced packages get their own UUID.

cards.title: Compiler-ready
cards.body: The LLM writes the meaning; the compiler builds the polished views.
